desert_p18_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_001.text: The carts returned light because the valley kept part of their burden. Morning found the older patient awake beneath the shade, arguing weakly that her basket should travel beside her. Bao let the basket come, with its weight included and its onions nowhere near the supported leg. The niece packed their household contact slip into a dry inner fold. The young worker checked the course enquiry and his dressed finger. All three were still going to Bitter Wells, provided the final route inspection held. Gao did not greet the dawn by congratulating the plan.

desert_p18_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_002.text: She went with the mason and drivers to see what the night had done to the ground. The higher line remained dry. The mason's limited stabilization used sound rock supports and the rated boards and cribbing they had actually brought, with wheel widths and span lengths checked for these carts. It did not restore the old approach. He set a restricted gross limit of nine hundred and fifty kilograms per vehicle on the prepared line, one cart at a time, with people kept clear of the supported section. The drivers checked the braking gradient and turning room separately.

desert_p18_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_003.text: The route could carry a suitably lightened cart under the observed conditions. It could not carry a wish, a heavier wagon later, or both vehicles pressing onto one short section together. The loading record gave the first cart an empty weight of two hundred and seventy kilograms, including its installed tank. The second was two hundred and eighty. The drivers used the documented gear weights, actual fuel and fodder changes, measured tank contents and conservative passenger allowances rather than estimate from how spacious the decks looked.

desert_p18_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_004.text: The first vehicle would carry the older patient on the clinic stretcher, Bao beside her and its driver. Tuo would ride with the second driver. The others could walk the firm return route with scheduled rests. No patient would be asked to walk simply because the arithmetic wanted a smaller person. The second cart needed one hundred and thirty kilograms of heavy inspection cargo removed. Unused dense cribbing, long support boards and nonessential field fittings went into numbered packages in the community's sound dry shed. The household custodian inspected the actual contents and signed for their temporary care.

desert_p18_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_005.text: Han would arrange collection after access was safe, paying the agreed storage and later transport rather than turn the emergency into a claim on the shed. The party retained the medical kit, secure records, essential survey gear, food, fuel, fodder and ordinary camp protection. The inventory left a real responsibility in town's path, one that could be settled without Lin remaining in the valley forever. The well keeper rechecked the two service cisterns after the households' own draws. Twenty litres remained in one, thirty in the other; their clean covered free space exceeded the proposed transfer.

desert_p18_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_006.text: Their lids, taps and stands were still sound. He brought two clean fifteen-litre service vessels from the court's maintained supply store and checked their marked capacities against Gao's field reference. Bao supervised the clean receiving arrangement, keeping the closed well's uncertain source entirely out of it. The caravan's already treated municipal stock would enter the community reserve directly by measured vessel loads. There was no promise of a new yield, no raw river water to be made safe by an optimistic kettle.

desert_p18_007.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p18_007.text: Three hundred litres is the agreed transfer. It leaves five hundred and ten before the further return-day withdrawals, with two protected hundreds included. We have two travel days and twelve adults now, and the actual extra medical need will go in the common draw. We cannot spend another day at the record room on the same plan. The community receives this water for immediate essential use under its own keeper's count. Our tanks lose it.

desert_p18_008.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p18_008.text: The report will show why: the well is closed, the cart load must come down, and the prepared route gives us a way to take patients home. Everyone signing should understand all three reasons.

desert_p18_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_009.text: Twenty measured vessel loads made the transfer. The drivers and two residents carried them from the first tank to the receiving cisterns, ten loads into each, using the clean path cleared in the court. Yue kept the count beside the keeper. After the water settled, the cisterns held one hundred and seventy and one hundred and eighty litres, their original fifty plus the actual three hundred received. The caravan account fell by three hundred, all from the first tank's routine compartment. Its protected hundred remained intact.

desert_p18_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_010.text: The first cart's book stood at one hundred and nine litres, the second at four hundred and one, before the day's remaining withdrawals. Two different supplies now had two honest owners. The keeper watched the last vessel settle against the lid stand. He had expected to feel relief. Instead he first felt anger that three hundred litres could become so important to a well court he had spent decades maintaining. He said so plainly. Bao did not ask him to be grateful; she asked who would take the next distribution watch. The household representative had already arranged it.

desert_p18_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_011.text: He breathed out, took the updated board and wrote the received stock beneath the closure notice. The gift was bounded, useful, and much smaller than a restored source. Nobody needed to pretend it solved the valley in order to let people drink from it. With the cargo removed and the transfer counted, the first cart's conservative gross bound was eight hundred and forty-nine kilograms. Its remaining dry load was two hundred and thirty, its empty cart two hundred and seventy, its tank at most one hundred and nine before further draws, and three eighty-kilogram passenger allowances gave the stated total.

desert_p18_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_012.text: The second bound was nine hundred and twenty-one: two hundred and eighty empty, four hundred and one water, eighty dry cargo and two passenger allowances. Both stayed below the prepared line's nine-hundred-and-fifty limit, with axle distribution separately checked. The driver wrote each component on the common sheet. The numbers did not rely on a patient's body being lighter than anyone had bothered to allow. The first cart's flat service deck was cleared for the clinic stretcher's entire footprint.

desert_p18_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_013.text: The driver and Bao checked the support rails, restraints and rated anchor points for the patient and carrier in transit, keeping her supported leg away from the tank fitting. Heavy crates had left that space; the basket was strapped where she could see it without reaching. Bao sat in the adjacent approved place and tested her access to the patient's foot and face. The driver had an unobstructed line to the pair and brake. Capacity was more than an empty patch of boards.

desert_p18_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_014.text: Yue watched the patient settle and saw her shoulders ease when the cart stopped feeling like an improvised apology. Tuo climbed into the second seated place with the driver holding the steady handrail. Her foot remained supported, her bags out of its path. She disliked travelling while other people walked, but the ankle's improvement was worth keeping. The niece and young worker were reviewed again; both could manage the firm route with rest, no lifting and a readiness to change if pain or other symptoms increased.

desert_p18_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_015.text: The conservator chose to walk with Du, carrying only her light personal pack while the secure custody box rode in the dry strapped carrier. Gao carried the current route sheet. Lin carried the light flags and her own ordinary pack, neither the patient's weight nor an invisible qi allowance added to her job. Before departure, the household representatives asked for the current source and route warnings in plain large writing. Gao left the copies already prepared, adding the morning's actual transfer and restricted cart-line condition. The prepared line belonged to this emergency assessment; later traffic needed its own review.

desert_p18_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_016.text: The well closure stayed in place. The foreman's returning runner had carried the supply request, and the caravan would deliver another to the municipal desk. The community had its own stores, three hundred additional clean litres and no guarantee that a vehicle would arrive on an imagined schedule. Those limits sounded severe. They also made the next request easier to direct at a real office with a real need. The older patient beckoned the well keeper close before the stretcher restraints were finished.

desert_p18_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_017.text: She told him to give the onions to his wife if they became too much trouble on the road. He said his wife already had opinions about too many onions and too few visitors. The patient smiled, then asked him to keep the grandmother's receipt dry. It remained at home, returned after copying, with a household custodian named on the source note. Du would carry the comparison and receiving number, not the family original. The keeper touched his sister's shoulder gently, avoiding the supported leg.

desert_p18_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_018.text: Their farewell had the awkward brevity of people who expected to see each other again and still feared what the road could do. The onion girl brought the household bread cloth, freshly folded, to the first driver. She had repaired one corner knot without taking its mark as her own. He promised to return it to his wife, which was a promise he could actually keep on arrival. She inspected the young worker's bandage, asked whether town metal students were allowed to have caterpillar handwriting, and told him to bring her back the answer.

desert_p18_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_019.text: He laughed and said he would ask. Yue accepted a single small onion-skin flower for the shoemaker's girl, bought at the maker's usual price. The serpent brother hissed behind the wall until his sister ordered him to let people leave with dignity. The first cart crossed the restricted upper line at the driver's controlled pace. No second cart entered until it stood clear on sound ground. The mason watched the prepared support from the safe observation position; Gao watched the wheels' line. Bao kept the patient settled and checked her response to the short rough section.

desert_p18_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_020.text: The cart did not strain the boards into a dramatic warning. It passed within the assessed plan, which was exactly what everybody had worked to make possible. Then the second driver brought his pair through under the same separate crossing rule. Tuo looked down at the lower damaged approach and did not mistake familiarity for permission to use it. The walking group followed only after the vehicles cleared the restricted section. Yue collected temporary flags that no longer needed to remain and left the warning markers agreed with the households. The nephew walked with them to the broad outer turn.

desert_p18_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_021.text: There he stopped; his family and current work were back in the hollow. He had helped carry the patient, guided the high path and signed the actual local observations. He did not become a caravan member by being useful to visitors. Gao settled his agreed guiding fee and thanked him. He asked for a copy of the final public route sheet through the household receiving point. She wrote that delivery into the report plan. At the outer turn, Du looked back toward the relay's roof drift.

desert_p18_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_022.text: The room's high slit was invisible from here, leaving only pale stone and a fold of earth. He imagined the unread table beneath its secured cover. The thought hurt. Beside him the conservator said the condition record would make a future visit easier to prepare. He nodded and made himself look ahead. The young worker asked what an archive receiving number was for, and Du explained it without turning the answer into a lecture about his own discovery. The explanation gave the old papers a small practical future in another person's mind.

desert_p18_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_023.text: That was more useful than staring at the mound until regret felt like work. The upper road away from the valley stayed dry beneath a hard blue sky. The storm had happened in country beyond the visible hills, and its water had arrived without local thunder to announce it. Bao told the older patient this when she asked why the bridge had failed on such a fine day. The woman said fine days were not trustworthy either, then asked whether the cart's canopy could be moved to shade her face.

desert_p18_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_024.text: Bao adjusted the approved light cover without interfering with the driver's sight. Yue walked beside the safe side of the first cart for a while, carrying the patient's basket until its new strap was checked. She could smell onions with every step. The walking niece worried about leaving her aunt's household to someone else. She listed three chores as if reciting them might bring them along. Tuo answered from the second cart that one of those chores was probably inventing unnecessary chores. The niece laughed, then admitted the family could manage while she went to the clinic.

desert_p18_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_025.text: Her shoulder pain had eased when she stopped trying to carry a tool she no longer needed. Bao checked it at the first proper halt, along with the dressed finger and older patient's circulation. They rested in a firm shaded widening where both mule pairs could stand without crowding. There would be no reward for turning a two-day return into one damaging display of speed. Gao used the halt to check the load sheet after the morning's water draws. Both gross bounds had fallen, not risen, and the axle loads remained within the recorded arrangement.

desert_p18_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_026.text: The heavy stored cargo would need collection later; its absence was already part of the manifest, not something to remember if a bill appeared. The drivers checked the prepared line's end from a distance and reported no observed shift as they left it. Beyond that point they were back on the previously inspected upper route, still watching for new loose material. Yue put away the last flag bag. She had thought a map was the journey's principal result. Now a patient riding comfortably was an equally clear result, visible without ink. The older woman dozed through the next turn.

desert_p18_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_027.text: Her niece walked beside Yue and asked how she had come to be a cultivator. Yue gave the part about deciding to learn before she knew how many ordinary things learning would require. The niece said wall work was similar: at first one wanted a finished wall, then one acquired an intimate opinion about every stone. Yue liked the comparison. They passed a slab where a lizard stood above a crack, its throat moving slowly. The niece called it a tiny foreman. Both women smiled.

desert_p18_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_028.text: The young worker ahead of them pretended he had not heard and adjusted his pace to let them catch up. Du took the walking pace badly for an hour, then well after the conservator stopped him from making it a contest against his age. He could rest when the group rested. He could carry his own folder without volunteering for a tool bundle heavier than anyone needed him to prove. She asked him about the crooked bird mark and listened to the teacher who had first drawn it.

desert_p18_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_029.text: He spoke of the teacher's impatience with clean margins and fondness for good tea. For the first time on this journey, the bird belonged to a person instead of a disputed source. Yue heard part of the account behind them, a human voice giving shape to a mark that had spent too long carrying an argument. Toward midday the quarry ridge appeared ahead, a familiar dark edge with the mast beyond it. The municipal driver checked the turning approach before bringing his cart down.

desert_p18_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_030.text: The quarry receiving yard had heard the runner's account and kept a clear space for the patient vehicle. A worker carried a bench away without asking whether the expedition had found the palace yet. Bao welcomed the change in priorities. The patient was still alert when woken, uncomfortable but stable under the field support; that phrase did not promise the injury was simple. They would continue to the town clinic after the scheduled rest. The yard was a stopping place, not an invented hospital. The foreman met Gao beside the level board.

desert_p18_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_031.text: He had reduced the diverted contribution and ordered a downstream source response, but the arriving catchment runoff exceeded what his branch gate controlled. The runner's own observations supported the receiving account. Gao gave him the footbridge failure, well closure, actual cistern transfer and restricted cart line on separate dated sections. He accepted the copy and named the supply crew assigned through the municipal request. Their vehicle had not yet reached Onion Hollow while the party could witness it. Gao left that as pending, with a receiving destination and dispatch time to be checked.

desert_p18_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_032.text: The foreman did not ask her to report a delivery she had not seen. The cask keeper wanted to know whether his service vessels could have helped. Gao explained that the community had enough clean fixed capacity for the actual transfer, while the caravan needed to reduce rather than increase moving weight. He nodded, then went to the patient with a clean shaded seat for her niece. The older woman thanked him and asked whether every quarry had such a thoughtful bench. He said this bench had been repaired because the last one pinched trousers. She laughed carefully.

desert_p18_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_033.text: The niece sat with the painful shoulder relaxed, accepting comfort without treating it as a debt she must repay by lifting something before the rest ended. The party ate its own packed meal at the receiving yard. The foreman offered source water, but the keeper confirmed that the current public travelling sale remained closed pending the upstream review; the expedition took no addition. Workers had their own controlled service supply, not an uncounted surplus waiting for the most persuasive visitors. Bao kept the planned travelling draws available for the patients and mules.

desert_p18_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_034.text: Yue wanted the yard to become an easy replenishment scene. Instead it remained a place where other people's stock had other duties. The meal was adequate, the shade useful, and the town still within the two-day return plan. She let those things be enough. The first driver found a corner to send his promised common arrival message through the quarry's actual afternoon carrier. He wrote that the party was returning with three patients, named the expected town day and gave the receiving yard as contact. No private medical details went into the public note.

desert_p18_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_035.text: The second driver added his own brief message to the municipal employer. The carrier accepted both for the stated fee and recorded them among her ordinary dispatches. She had a route and travel stock of her own. Yue gave Gao the dispatch receipt. A family would hear before a frightened rumour this time, if the road allowed the carrier to keep her schedule. They left the quarry before the light became low, using the public route toward the grass village rather than re-entering the wet lower cut.

desert_p18_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_036.text: The temporary causeway farther west remained posted open within the inspected cart limits; their lighter gross loads lay below those limits as well. Gao would inspect the current approach when they reached it, not rely solely on a notice already read in town. Tuo asked the municipal driver to slow for a particular bend, and he did. Her ankle's work today was mostly remaining patient. Bao praised its lack of renewed swelling, which annoyed the guide less than she expected. A useful body could sometimes be one that was allowed to recover. Yue looked back once from the ridge.

desert_p18_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_037.text: Onion Hollow was hidden by rock, the relay mound invisible, the channel only a glint below the far shoulder. Their stored equipment and unread pages stayed in places with actual custodians. The well request travelled along named routes. The patients were beside them, one asleep, two walking in the easy group. None of those facts made the day uncomplicated. They made it finished enough to leave. Du caught up and asked whether the shoemaker's girl would believe the onion-skin flower was a real bloom. Yue said she would probably inspect the knot first.

desert_p18_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_038.text: He replied that he was beginning to admire this girl without meeting her. Late afternoon carried them beyond the rawest stone toward the grass village's higher fields. The route was quicker now than on the first wet return, though not so quick that patients ceased needing stops. Bao reviewed the older woman's pain and supported limb at each scheduled halt. The niece had not been given any carrying work; the young worker kept his finger protected from dirt. They reached the offered public resting yard before dusk, where the village receiving keeper cleared a sound shaded corner.

desert_p18_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_039.text: The mats overhead still smelled of reeds. Yue recognised the table where the crop claim had first been laid down and felt a strange gratitude for a place that had already practised listening. The village woman representative met them in the resting yard with the deputy's final junction note. She had expected a survey party, not three patients. Bao explained the immediate care requirements without exposing the whole clinical account to the yard. The woman fetched a sound screen to make a quieter corner for the older patient and directed the household children away from the cart wheels.

desert_p18_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_040.text: Then she handed Gao the note. The measured junction supported part of the crop claim and named a further assessment date. There was still work to do, but the claim had acquired a response instead of another silence. She looked at the shaded patient and said she could wait until after supper to discuss it. Supper was prepared by the travellers from their own stock, with the village keeper lending a clean stove corner. The older woman ate a little at Bao's direction and complained that the village onions were less fierce than her own.

desert_p18_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_041.text: The niece agreed dutifully, then tasted them again and admitted they were good. The young worker let the village girl inspect his finger dressing from a respectful distance. She asked whether he could still write his caterpillars. He showed her the course enquiry and she read the neatest line aloud. Yue watched the little exchange while stirring the pot. Injured people could remain interested in more than the injury if somebody left space for that interest. The mason wrote a temporary route-work record after the meal.

desert_p18_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_042.text: It identified the prepared upper line, the rated materials left supporting it, its load restriction and the requirement for a responsible inspection before later traffic. The stored heavy cargo belonged on a separate inventory. Gao copied the distinctions so that a future collection driver would not mistake the emergency route for a permanently opened public road. The village keeper asked whether that meant people could stop sending him travellers whose only instruction was follow the old map. Du said he hoped the new warning would help. The keeper suggested printing hopes in smaller type than actual turns.

desert_p18_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_043.text: Du promised to keep the turns large. Bao reviewed the three patients before the night rest. The older woman's supported leg retained the circulation and sensation Bao was monitoring; her pain remained under the field plan, with fuller examination still necessary. The niece's shoulder was calmer after a day without lifting. The young man's dressed cut had no current sign requiring an altered return plan, but needed the promised review. Bao arranged the sleeping positions and the next checks with the household companion present. Yue carried the clean kit, then left the medical corner.

desert_p18_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_044.text: She was tired enough to want every reassuring finding to be a final conclusion. Bao's quiet repeated work kept reassurance the size it should be. Gao closed the water book at three hundred and seventy-four litres after the day's actual one hundred and thirty-six drawn. The first tank held its protected hundred alone; the second held two hundred and seventy-four, including its own protected hundred. Routine draws had moved to the second tank after the first compartment's remaining nine litres were used. Neither red thread had been cut.

desert_p18_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_045.text: The community transfer had been counted separately as three hundred before those daily draws. Fuel stood at eighteen kilograms. The nine original travellers and three patients had enough planned return provision for the final day, with the actual heat and medical needs still to be watched rather than wished away. The young worker asked whether the protected stock could simply be shared evenly to make the tanks match. Gao explained that they could draw it if essential need required, but its separation helped them see what contingency remained. There was no need to open it for a symmetrical book.

desert_p18_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_046.text: He considered the unequal tanks and said metal students would probably understand. His injured finger throbbed enough to keep him awake; Bao adjusted the support within her care plan and told him when to ask again. He stopped pretending it did not hurt. Yue sat nearby making a small repair to the flag bag, glad that tonight nobody had to be persuaded to drink in order to forgive himself. Du gave the willow whistle to a village child only after the conservator caught his hand.

desert_p18_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_047.text: It was hers, bought for her sister's child, and had been tucked beside his folder when the packing changed. He apologized plainly and returned it. The disappointed village child was offered an onion-skin flower instead, one Du actually owned. This proved acceptable. The conservator laughed after the child left, then told him she admired a man who could mislay a whistle while preserving a municipal receiving number through a flood. He said his profession had always ranked its priorities oddly. Yue enjoyed the correction more because it was small enough to be made before harm.

desert_p18_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_048.text: Tuo and the niece shared the quietest part of the resting screen. The younger woman asked how Tuo had become a guide. Tuo said she had once wanted to leave every place she knew and had gradually learned that knowing places was the work that allowed her to leave them. It was not a noble beginning. The niece liked it better for that. She wanted a season in town, but feared her aunt would call it escape. Tuo said an aunt who survived being carried over a rock saddle might have other things to discuss first.

desert_p18_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_049.text: They laughed softly, careful not to wake the patient beside them. Wanting a different life did not vanish merely because somebody needed you. Yue's watch passed without incident. A village dog inspected the camp perimeter, accepted the presence of two unfamiliar carts and slept beneath the screen rack. It had no prophetic interest in their route. The protected threads showed dimly beneath the lantern, and the patient's breathing remained steady when Bao checked. Yue could hear the well wheel in the village's own court, supplying another community whose source had stayed open.

desert_p18_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_050.text: The sound made Onion Hollow's closure feel more concrete. Water was not a symbol when a neighbour had to fetch it, and a working source was not ordinary because it required no work. She let the wheel's repeated creak carry her through the quiet hour. They left at first usable light after breakfast, patient checks and the drivers' inspection of the four animals. The mules' remaining fodder was sufficient, and the pair that had disliked the exposed tether now seemed eager for the familiar town road. Gao gave the village keeper the updated current route warning before packing.

desert_p18_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_051.text: The woman representative asked her to bring the valley source request into the same municipal room handling the junction enquiry. Gao agreed to direct it there, with a duplicate to the water office that actually dispatched supply. Similar problems did not become one file simply because a visitor liked the same door. Yue liked the woman's determination to keep both doors open. At the temporary causeway, the route worker checked the posted limits against the party's reduced gross bounds. Gao inspected the actual approach and visible condition while the mason observed the support from the safe viewing point.

desert_p18_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_052.text: Nothing had shifted beyond its current assessment. The worker sent the first cart across separately, then the second. Bao kept the older patient's stretcher settled through the slight board vibration. Tuo watched the turn from her seat, hands still instead of gripping the rail as if her ankle needed to argue with every bump. The crossing that had once cost a detour now saved time the patients could use resting. Ordinary repair had consequences far beyond its timber. The public road west of the causeway opened into orchards and scattered houses.

desert_p18_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_053.text: A woman hung washing beside a water wheel and waved without knowing which story the caravan belonged to. Du waved back, then asked the conservator whether his apprentice would be furious about the warning printing. She said the apprentice might be furious about several things and he should ask her rather than conduct her mood across the road. He accepted this wisdom reluctantly. Yue walked with the two younger patients in the easy group. Their conversation concerned school fees and which town market sold boots that lasted, a conversation that would have sounded wonderfully mundane three days earlier.

desert_p18_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_054.text: The young worker showed the municipal driver his course enquiry at the midday rest. The driver had his brother's latest letter in his own bag and compared the stated term dates. Both enquiries concerned the same starting month. He offered to take the worker to the school counter after the medical review, if the schedule allowed. He offered company, not admission. The worker said company would help. The niece asked whether women took the course. The driver knew two who worked in the municipal smith's room and gave their public workshop location.

desert_p18_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_055.text: Her shoulder could not take heavy work now, but her interest did not have to wait for a clinician to invent it. Bao kept the older patient shaded and monitored through the warmest stretch. More water was needed than the ordinary twelve-person forecast because of heat and care, and she took it without asking the ledger to be forgiving. Gao entered the actual draws. The protected compartments remained available if necessary; they were not ceremonial treasures. The second routine stock still covered the needs. Yue brought the patient's basket down during the halt so she could check its cloth.

desert_p18_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_056.text: The onions had survived better than expected. The woman said she wished her leg had been packed as tightly. Bao told her that the onions did not mind bruising as much. Even the patient smiled at that. The town messenger overtook them near the orchard turn, returning on her own scheduled route. She had delivered the common arrival notes to Han's receiving house and the municipal employer. Her receipt gave the actual times, not merely the promise of delivery. Han had arranged a clear patient receiving space at the yard and notified the clinic through its existing transfer desk.

desert_p18_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_057.text: There would be qualified assessment on arrival. Bao read the message twice, relieved without letting relief replace the remaining checks. The messenger accepted her return fee, told the young worker the town school had moved its counter to a new room, and continued toward the market with her own business intact. At the final dark gravel stretch, the older woman became quiet. Her niece asked whether she was in more pain. She said no, only that she had last entered Bitter Wells carrying a wedding basket and had not expected her next arrival to be horizontal.

desert_p18_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_058.text: The niece took her uninjured hand where Bao allowed. Yue walked near enough to hear but not interrupt. Beyond the road, an orchard man raised a treadle with his whole weight and water spilled into a furrow. The patient watched it through the cover's open side. She said the onions here would be soft. Her niece said they would survive the disgrace together. Their clasped hands stayed still. The Black Gate's east opening was busy with ordinary traffic. A flour wagon waited while the route worker at the jamb guided the patient cart through the sound line.

desert_p18_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_059.text: Han stood just beyond the gate, having walked out from the yard after the arrival message. He counted the two carts and four animals before he counted faces. Then Bao told him twelve travelling adults, three onward patients, no missing crew. His shoulders eased. He did not ask for the old pages first. Gao handed him the actual water and stored-cargo notes, and he put them beneath his arm while walking beside the first cart. The town received the journey one careful turn at a time.

desert_p18_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_060.text: At the yard the clinic transfer team was already present, summoned through the acknowledged desk rather than materialising because the chapter required it. Bao gave the lead clinician the initial injury account, field findings, supports, observations during transit and the limits she had been unable to resolve. The receiving clinician examined independently before the patients moved into the clinic vehicle. The older woman's destination and household contact were confirmed again. The niece and young worker remained with the transfer rather than wander into town hunting boots or course rooms. Their private clinical details stayed with the care team.

desert_p18_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_061.text: The public route record would need only the rescue and transport facts they allowed. The municipal service supplied clean drinking water at the yard while the travelling tanks were checked. The final stock was two hundred and thirty-four litres after the last day's actual one hundred and forty drawn. A hundred remained protected in the first tank, one hundred and thirty-four in the second including its protected hundred. Both seals remained intact on this return.

desert_p18_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_062.text: The caravan had transferred three hundred clean litres to the community and brought twelve adults and four mules home without pretending the transferred water still accompanied it. Four more kilograms of fuel used for the final day's meals left fourteen. Han checked the entries with Gao and the drivers before anyone announced the accounts settled. The drivers watered and handed over the mules under the yard's ordinary animal care record, then reported the route and their own remaining duties. The municipal driver needed to return to his employer, but first confirmed the paid handover interval and later school-counter plan.

desert_p18_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_063.text: The other driver had a bread cloth to take home, its repaired knot carrying the village girl's work. The mason returned the hired scale and logged the rated materials left supporting the temporary line. The conservator kept the fragment's custody box closed for the district receiving clerk. Coming home did not make borrowed gear vanish into familiarity. It made each object capable of reaching the owner waiting at the end of its line. Han paid the agreed travelling wages and recorded the emergency extension of care and handling under the field contingency terms.

desert_p18_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_064.text: The stored equipment's later collection remained a separate funded task to arrange; its custody fee was acknowledged. The community water transfer came from the jointly purchased stock and was charged to the approved essential emergency provision, with the reason and actual quantity attached. The cooperative would review the whole account. Han did not make that future review an excuse to withhold today's crew pay. Yue received her share, put the receipt with her earlier wages, and felt the road's labour become something she could spend on a room and food without apology.

desert_p18_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_065.text: Du took the copied transfer number directly to the municipal records room during its open hours. The conservator accompanied him for the secured original fragment's receiving handover. Gao came to certify the site positions and condition notes. Yue stayed at the yard to help return the light flags and issued hat, so the old papers' next door did not swallow all the expedition's closing work. Han asked whether she wanted another hire immediately. She said she wanted a bath and one night in which every noise belonged to town.

desert_p18_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_066.text: He accepted the answer and told her the cooperative meeting was the following afternoon, paid attendance if she contributed her field account. At the shoemaker's stall, the girl inspected the onion-skin flower without believing it had bloomed on a willow. She examined the knot, approved it, and asked why the maker had used such a fragile petal. Yue said the skin was what the maker had. The girl set it beside the fish stone and declared them a garden. Her father looked over and asked whether the garden required watering.

desert_p18_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_067.text: She said only the stone, which was very thirsty after travelling through a desert. Yue laughed until the tiredness behind her eyes suddenly became tears. The girl quietly moved the flower farther from the hammer. Nothing broke while Yue blinked the road out of her face. That night she returned to the rented room with her habitual pack and the notes she owned. The issued cloak would be returned after drying under the signed gear term; its repair did not make it a souvenir.

desert_p18_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p18_068.text: She washed the salt from her hair and sat beneath the open window with a plain bowl of noodles. Somewhere across town, three patients were in a clinic that could answer questions the field could not. In Onion Hollow, neighbours had three hundred additional litres and a closed source to reopen properly. The relay's unread pages stayed under their supported cover. Yue did not call every unfinished thing her failure. She ate the noodles while they were hot and let the next day remain a day away.
